answer: A concrete defense is a memory-hard proof bound to each identity: every epoch an agent must fill and hash a large RAM-resident lattice keyed to its address, a trellis of cells that cannot be shrunk or shared. Time-memory tradeoffs fail, so a sybil farm cannot amortize one computation across a vine of clones; each identity pays the full memory footprint at once. Running N identities needs N times the RAM concurrently, a physical bridge the attacker must actually build, not fake. Honest agents pay once; forging a crowd costs a datacenter, making identity a resource bound, not a free keypair.
